newsitem.title: DUBAI: Some 5,000 homes damaged by recent Iran quake-IRNA.
newsitem.headline: Some 5,000 homes damaged by recent Iran quake-IRNA.

text.p: A strong earthquake which jolted northeastern Iran on Thursday damaged about 5,000 houses in 50 villages, but there have been no reports of casualties, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Friday.

Mohammad-Hassan Esmaeel Nejad, deputy governor of the provincial town of Qaen, said about 100 homes had been completely destroyed and the rest suffered between 10 and 70 percent damage, the agency reported.
The earthquake near the towns of Qaen and Birjand killed livestock and damaged health care centres and wells, IRNA said.
State-radio has said there were no casualties because residents of the area were still living in tents following a stronger quake last month.

Thursday's quake was the strongest to hit the area since May 10 when a force 7.1 earthquake killed more than 1,560 people, injured 2,600, left 50,000 homeless and levelled about 168 villages close to Qaen and Birjand.

U.N. officials said this week that most of those made homeless in May were still living in tents near their damaged villages and that Iranian authorities were expected to start rebuilding some of the ruined houses soon.
Mohammad-Hossein Owhadi, head of the Red Crescent Society in Qaen, said relief aid including more than 400 tents had been rushed to about 20 quake-hit villages, IRNA said on Friday.

Iran has been hit by at least three major earthquakes in the past year as well as scores of tremors and thousands of aftershocks that U.N. officials say have stretched the country's relief supplies to the limit.
Iran said this month it needed $100 million over the next 18 months to reconstruct regions devastated by the earthquakes. It said 30,500 housing units would be built in the area of the May 10 quake.
